claim: The mechanism of nonenzymatic polymerization is less well understood than enzymatic DNA/RNA polymerization, despite its critical role in the origin of life.
source: The importance of genome replication has inspired detailed crystallographic studies of enzymatic DNA/RNA polymerization. In contrast, the mechanism of nonenzymatic polymerization is less well understood, despite its critical role in the origin of life.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the state of knowledge in the field, drawing on established scientific understanding.

claim: Nonenzymatic RNA primer extension was directly observed through time-resolved crystallography.
source: Here we report the direct observation of nonenzymatic RNA primer extension through time-resolved crystallography.
evidence: The abstract states this as a primary finding of the study.

claim: Crystals of an RNA primer-template-dGMP complex were soaked with guanosine-5′-phosphoro-2-aminoimidazolide for increasing times.
source: We soaked crystals of an RNA primer-template-dGMP complex with guanosine-5′-phosphoro-2-aminoimidazolide for increasing times.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: At early times, activated ribonucleotides are bound to the template.
source: At early times we see the activated ribonucleotides bound to the template, followed by formation of the imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate.
evidence: This describes observations from the time-resolved crystallography experiments.

claim: Formation of the imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate follows the binding of activated ribonucleotides to the template.
source: At early times we see the activated ribonucleotides bound to the template, followed by formation of the imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate.
evidence: This describes the temporal sequence of events observed in the crystallography experiments.

claim: At later times, a new phosphodiester bond forms between the primer and the incoming nucleotide.
source: At later times, we see a new phosphodiester bond forming between the primer and the incoming nucleotide.
evidence: This describes observations from later time points in the crystallography experiments.

claim: The intermediate is pre-organized because of the constraints of base-pairing with the template and hydrogen bonding between the imidazole amino group and both flanking phosphates.
source: The intermediate is pre-organized because of the constraints of base-pairing with the template and hydrogen bonding between the imidazole amino group and both flanking phosphates.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data obtained from the crystallography experiments.

claim: Many lines of evidence point to a central role for RNA in the emergence of life on Earth.
source: Many lines of evidence point to a central role for RNA in the emergence of life on Earth (Sutherland, 2016; Wachowius et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to other scholarly work.

claim: The earliest forms of life must have replicated their simple RNA genomes without the aid of complex enzymes.
source: As part of the RNA world hypothesis, the earliest forms of life must have replicated their simple RNA genomes without the aid of complex enzymes (Orgel, 2004).
evidence: This is a theoretical claim supported by citation to the RNA world hypothesis.

claim: A key part of early life replication would have been the nonenzymatic template directed polymerization of activated RNA nucleotides.
source: A key part of this process would have been the nonenzymatic template directed polymerization of activated RNA nucleotides.
evidence: This is an inference based on the RNA world hypothesis.

claim: The local conformation at the reaction site greatly impacts the nonenzymatic RNA polymerization reaction.
source: Previous studies have suggested that the local conformation at the reaction site greatly impacts the nonenzymatic RNA polymerization reaction.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from previous studies.

claim: A wide range of nucleic acid backbones, such as peptide or threose nucleic acids, can template the polymerization of activated RNA monomers.
source: For example, a wide range of nucleic acid backbones, such as peptide (Schmidt et al., 1997) or threose nucleic acids (Heuberger and Switzer, 2006), can template the polymerization of activated RNA monomers, but the fastest reactions occur on A-form structured RNA or LNA templates (Zielinski et al., 2000; Schrum et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The fastest nonenzymatic polymerization reactions occur on A-form structured RNA or LNA templates.
source: For example, a wide range of nucleic acid backbones, such as peptide (Schmidt et al., 1997) or threose nucleic acids (Heuberger and Switzer, 2006), can template the polymerization of activated RNA monomers, but the fastest reactions occur on A-form structured RNA or LNA templates (Zielinski et al., 2000; Schrum et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The A-form conformation of the template provides a structure conducive for the polymerization reaction.
source: These results indicate that the A-form conformation of the template provides a structure conducive for the polymerization reaction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited experimental results.

claim: Downstream helper oligomers are commonly utilized to improve the yield of primer extension reactions.
source: Downstream helper oligomers, commonly utilized to improve the yield of primer extension reactions, are also thought to improve the reaction in part by stabilizing the A-form structure of an otherwise disordered ssRNA template (Vogel et al., 2005; Prywes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Downstream helper oligomers improve the reaction in part by stabilizing the A-form structure of an otherwise disordered ssRNA template.
source: Downstream helper oligomers, commonly utilized to improve the yield of primer extension reactions, are also thought to improve the reaction in part by stabilizing the A-form structure of an otherwise disordered ssRNA template (Vogel et al., 2005; Prywes et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation supported by citations.

claim: Structural aspects of the template near the reaction site may underlie many of the characteristics of nonenzymatic RNA polymerization, such as the rate and fidelity of polymerization.
source: Structural aspects of the template near the reaction site may underlie many of the characteristics of nonenzymatic RNA polymerization, such as the rate and fidelity of polymerization (Leu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citation.

claim: Nucleoside-5′-phosphoro-imidazolide substrates are too labile to use directly in crystallographic studies.
source: However, the widely used nucleoside-5′-phosphoro-imidazolide substrates are too labile to use directly in crystallographic studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the chemical properties of these substrates based on experimental knowledge.

claim: Stable phosphonate analogs have been utilized, co-crystallized with a primer template duplex, to help model the structure of the reaction site.
source: We have instead utilized stable phosphonate analogs, co-crystallized with a primer template duplex, to help model the structure of the reaction site (Zhang et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes previous work by the authors, supported by citations.

source: In contrast, the symmetrical 5′−5′ triphosphate-linked dinucleotide GpppG, which is an analogue of the imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate, was observed in a crystal structure to bind the template through two consecutive Watson-Crick base-pairs, with the 3′-hydroxyl of the primer positioned for in-line attack (Zhang et al., 2017).

claim: The high reactivity of the imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate could be due to a favorable preorganized geometry in the template bound state.

source: Consistent with this model, the superiority of the newly identified nucleotide-5′-phosphoro-2-aminoimidazolide (2-AIpN) monomers (Li et al., 2017), is thought to be due to the greater stability of the corresponding imidazolium-bridged dinucleotide intermediate (Np-AI-pN) (Walton and Szostak, 2017).

claim: Helper oligonucleotides pre-organize the reaction site and decrease the distance between the 3′-hydroxyl of the primer and the phosphate of the adjacent nucleotide.

claim: Time-resolved X-ray crystallography has been greatly developed to study the dynamic processes of macromolecules and small molecules.

claim: Catalytic activity is sometimes preserved in crystallized proteins.
